entities.name: PMID:25092651
observations: Purified L. interrogans heme oxygenase (LepHO) degraded heme in vitro; plastidic-type ferredoxin-NADP(+) reductase (LepFNR) supplied electrons and drove complete degradation to free iron and alpha-biliverdin.
The authors conclude heme-iron scavenging by LepHO requires LepFNR as its redox partner; evidence is biochemical rather than a LepFNR loss-of-function growth test.

entities.name: PMID:18524663
observations: A hemO transposon mutant of L. interrogans grew poorly when hemoglobin was the sole iron source, and purified HemO degraded heme in vitro.
This provides genetic and biochemical evidence that functional heme oxygenase is required for efficient hemoglobin-derived iron utilization.

entities.name: PMID:19114124
observations: The hemO mutant showed attenuated hamster disease, supporting a role for heme oxygenase in pathogenesis and heme as an in vivo iron source.

entities.name: LepHO
observations: L. interrogans heme oxygenase catalyzes heme turnover and releases iron; hemO disruption impairs growth with hemoglobin as the sole iron source.

entities.name: LepFNR
observations: L. interrogans plastidic-type ferredoxin-NADP(+) reductase provides reducing electrons directly to LepHO and supports complete heme degradation in vitro without ferredoxin.
